messages:
sam_support: customer reported large tail latency spikes on embeddings after they flipped on dynamic batching yesterday. they see ~200ms median but tails up to 2s. also intermittent 400s: "Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 128". attaching logs.

sam_support: here's the minimal repro curl they sent: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["short text","longer text blob ..."],"meta":{"client_batch_hint":true}}'
```

sam_support: logs show repeated lines: `batcher: drained early (size=6,max=64,timeout_ms=20)` then a few `reject: dim_mismatch` errors. customer says they use mixed client SDKs (js + python) during rollout.

ingrid_engineer: thanks — couple of things to check quickly: are they accidentally sending precomputed vectors in some requests? dimension mismatch message implies some payloads are being interpreted as vectors instead of raw inputs, or they're hitting a different model.

ingrid_engineer: can we get a request_id from one of the 400s? sam, any example request_id?

sam_support: support-bot uploaded the logs: https://s3.redwood/sess/1767001234/logs.tar.gz :session_id=acme-378. sample request_id=acme-378-req-00042.

alex_runtime: looked at the logs. pattern: a flurry of tiny requests (1 token inputs) interleaved with a couple of large text blobs. dynamic batcher configured with `max_batch_size=64` and `batch_timeout_ms=10`. small requests hit the fast-path and fill batches quickly, causing the batcher to drain very often. large requests that arrive just after a drain wait until the next fill -> gets coalesced into a later batch and increases per-request tail. also one of the python clients was calling the embeddings endpoint with `input` as a precomputed numpy array (dimension 128) due to an internal feature flag; server saw that as a vector and threw dim mismatch.

maria_oncall: +1 on both causes. two mitigations: 1) set `batch_timeout_ms` to a slightly higher value (30-50ms) so large requests have a chance to join an in-flight batch; 2) set `batch_priorities`: small-requests -> latency priority, large-requests -> throughput priority OR split by header. For immediate customer-facing workaround: increase batch_timeout to 40ms and bump `max_batch_size` to 128 to reduce drain frequency.

sam_support: customer asked if dynamic batching should be disabled while they fix client bug. is that safe?

alex_runtime: disabling dynamic batching will make each request be handled individually or fall back to static batching config depending on route. it will avoid the fast-path drain behavior but will increase CPU/GPU cost. If they need a quick stopgap, yes disable dynamic batching and set a conservative `max_batch_size=32` on the route. also enable `reject_on_dim_mismatch=true` (explicit) so we catch precomputed-vector vs raw input earlier and return clearer errors to client SDKs.

maria_oncall: I'll prepare a patch we can push to the customer's Dedicated config: 
```
batching: {
  dynamic: false,
  max_batch_size: 32,
  batch_timeout_ms: 40,
  reject_on_dim_mismatch: true
}
```

maria_oncall: that should buy them time while their devs remove the feature flag that sends precomputed vectors. also recommend they upgrade python SDK to v1.8 which adds a validation warning when `input` looks like a vector.

sam_support: shared the recommended config and SDK upgrade. customer applied the change and reported tail p95 dropped from ~1200ms to ~220ms within 5 minutes. they still saw a single dim_mismatch error after deploy.

ingrid_engineer: for long-term: we should add a small internal heuristic: if >10% of batch elements are precomputed-vector-shaped, and dims don't match route-model, tag and reject earlier with richer error and a hint: "did you pass precomputed vectors? upgrade SDK v1.8 to auto-detect". we also might provide a per-route `batching.split_on_vector_payload` toggle.

alex_runtime: agree. i'll file an RFC for `split_on_vector_payload` and `adaptive_timeout` where the batcher increases timeout if it detects pending large payloads. will include perf numbers.

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0427-176700 (linked to acme-378).

sam_support: customer happy for now. closing once they confirm no further 400s. thanks team :thumbsup:
